calls.head: Nowhere to hide for MacKinnon
calls.body: At home, the Blue Jackets keep sending Knies’s line (Knies, Coyle and Olivier) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Rick Bowness has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Avalanche’s first line is Lehkonen, MacKinnon and Nečas.

calls.head: Expect the Avalanche to have the puck more
calls.body: The Avalanche have been one of the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Blue Jackets around the middle. Expect the Avalanche to spend more of the night in the Blue Jackets’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

surprises.head: Columbus found the good looks for once
surprises.body: Colorado is one of the league’s best at preventing dangerous shots. Not tonight: Columbus’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 10.0% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.3% (about 6.0% against Colorado) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 175 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

surprises.head: Columbus hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Columbus’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 42, against their usual 105 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 80 games.

story.head: Nichushkin scores against his old team
paras: Mathieu Olivier struck first for the Blue Jackets just 28 seconds into the game, and Ivan Provorov pushed the lead to 2-0 on the power play early in the first. Cale Makar got the Avalanche on the board less than four minutes later. There were five goals in the second period alone. Jake Christiansen and Cole Sillinger scored just over three minutes apart early in the period to make it 4-1. Colorado pulled Scott Wedgewood after four goals and turned to Mackenzie Blackwood for the rest of the second. Charlie Coyle stretched the lead to 5-1 on the power play midway through the second. Valeri Nichushkin made it 6-1, 39 seconds later, in his first game against Colorado since leaving. Nazem Kadri cut Columbus’ lead to 6-2 on the power play just under four minutes later. Coyle scored his second of the night midway through the third to make it 7-2 for the Blue Jackets. Olivier finished with a goal and two assists, and Coyle added two assists for a four-point night.

Don’t let the score fool you: the chances were a lot closer than that. Cam Talbot made 27 saves for the Blue Jackets. The Jackets moved to 6-7-0 and climbed off the bottom of the Metropolitan to sixth, while the Avalanche dropped to 9-6-1, slipping to fourth in the Central.
